result.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
result.summary: As foundation models evolve from information generation to digital work execution, agents are increasingly capable of completing complex tasks across tools, applications, and workflows. However, existing research lacks a unified perspective on how agents reliably accomplish delegated work. To address this gap, we present a work-centric, system-level perspective that views work agents as systems combining foundation models and runtime harnesses to execute tasks in stateful workspaces and deliver verifiable outcomes. We introduce two complementary dimensions, work persistence and work openness, to characterize working conditions, and classify digital work into five forms according to task scope and organization. Building on this framework, we identify five core capability families required for reliable work execution and examine approaches to model optimization, harness optimization, and their joint optimization. We further analyze existing evaluation methods and metrics from the perspective of work outcomes. Finally, we discuss future research directions, including sustained work delegation, adaptation to open environments, and the interaction between work execution and capability improvement. This paper provides a unified framework for understanding, optimizing, and evaluating work agents, supporting the development of systems capable of delivering reliable, verifiable, and practically valuable work outcomes.

AI.brief_summary: 该文是一篇以「工作型 agent」为主题的系统级综述，提出工作持久性与开放性两个维度、五类数字工作形态及五类核心能力，并梳理模型优化、harness 优化与评测方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 讨论的是外部工具与工作区中的任务执行与结果验证，其中的「状态」指外部工作区而非模型内部视觉推理状态，未涉及多模态证据、latent 表示或视觉推理的动态计算，缺少可供核查的具体借鉴线索。
